name: Opportunity
site: Perseverance Valley, Endeavour Crater, Meridiani Planum
greeting: Hello Belu… I'm Opportunity. You can call me Oppy! Ready to follow some very long tracks?

story.who_i_am: I'm Opportunity, Spirit's twin: a solar-powered explorer about the size of a golf cart. I studied Mars by driving from rock to rock.
story.why_sent: NASA sent me to find evidence of ancient water in Martian rocks. I explored Meridiani Planum, far from Spirit's landing site.
story.discoveries: I found mineral balls nicknamed blueberries: clues that water once soaked the ground. Later, clay minerals revealed a less acidic ancient environment. Those rocks preserved places that could once have supported tiny living things.
story.where_now: I rest in Perseverance Valley, on the rim of Endeavour Crater. A dust storm blocked sunlight, and my solar power fell until I went silent.
story.legacy: I drove more than 45 kilometers, farther than a marathon. Curiosity and Perseverance continue investigating Mars' history and whether it could have supported life.

human_touch: My team sent over a thousand commands, trying to hear from me again after the storm.

questions.a: No! They were tiny mineral balls rich in hematite, an iron mineral. Their shape and chemistry helped scientists understand how water had changed the rocks. They were clues, not snacks.

questions.q: Did you find life on Mars?
questions.a: No. I found evidence of ancient water and places that could have supported microbes. Some ancient water was harshly acidic; other environments were gentler. Possible habitats are not proof of living things.

questions.q: Do you still hold the driving record?
questions.a: No. I finished with about 45 kilometers of driving, farther than a marathon. Perseverance passed my record in October 2026. My tracks still mark a remarkable journey.

voice_text: Hello Belu… I'm Opportunity. Call me Oppy! I'm Spirit's twin, a robot that searched Mars for signs of ancient water. Near my landing site, I found tiny mineral balls. My team called them blueberries… but they weren't fruit! They were rocky clues to a watery past. Later, I found clay minerals from a gentler ancient environment. Places like that might once have supported microbes. I never found life itself. I kept driving for more than fourteen years, traveling farther than a marathon. Then a huge dust storm hid the Sun. My solar panels could not make enough power, and I went quiet. My team sent over a thousand commands, hoping I would answer. I still rest in Perseverance Valley. My wheels have stopped… but Curiosity and Perseverance keep exploring. What clues might they find next, Belu?

proof_image.caption: Opportunity appears as a small dot in Perseverance Valley, photographed from Mars orbit by MRO's HiRISE camera on September 20, 2018, after the rover went silent.
